content: Sulfasalazine is a medication prescribed to treat ulcerative colitis, a type of inflammatory bowel disease. While it does not cure the condition, it helps alleviate symptoms such as fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. Additionally, it is used to prolong the time between disease flare-ups after an acute attack has been managed. In its delayed-release form, sulfasalazine is also utilized to treat rheumatoid arthritis by reducing joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. Early treatment of rheumatoid arthritis with this medication can help prevent further joint damage, enabling patients to maintain their daily activities. This medication should be taken orally after meals with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) as directed by your doctor. To minimize stomach upset, your doctor may recommend gradually increasing the dosage when starting treatment. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to therapy. If you are taking the delayed-release tablets, swallow them whole without crushing, chewing, or breaking them. It is important to stay hydrated during treatment unless otherwise instructed by your doctor. Take this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Inform your doctor if your condition does not improve or worsens. Common side effects of sulfasalazine include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache, dizziness, or unusual fatigue. It may also cause your skin and urine to turn an orange-yellow color, which is harmless. Rarely, delayed-release tablets may appear whole or partially dissolved in your stool. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, in rare cases, it may cause severe allergic reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome), blood disorders (e.g., agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia), liver damage, nerve or muscle problems, and infections. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking sulfasalazine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, sulfa drugs, aspirin, related drugs (e.g., salicylates, NSAIDs like ibuprofen), mesalamine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Sulfasalazine may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, so limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication is similar to aspirin and may temporarily affect male fertility. During pregnancy, sulfasalazine should only be used when clearly necessary. Caution is advised if it is used near the expected delivery date, as similar drugs may harm a newborn. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Sulfasalazine may lower folic acid levels, increasing the risk of spinal cord defects. Ensure you are taking adequate folic acid as directed by your doctor. This drug passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Sulfasalazine is very similar to mesalamine. It may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine normetanephrine levels, liver function tests), potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctor that you are using this medication. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, liver/kidney function tests) should be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for proper disposal. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
